title: Adaptive credit vaults for tiered routing and quota prioritization
creator: Lina Patel
description:
Problem: Free-tier traffic bursts can starve paid and enterprise customers during global events, and simple per-tenant quotas lead to poor tail-latency behavior when pools saturate. We need a quota-aware tier-routing system that preserves SLOs for paid/enterprise while still offering acceptable experience for free users.

Proposal: Implement an 'Adaptive Credit Vault' subsystem that: (1) maintains per-plan credit reservoirs (free/paid/enterprise) with configurable soft reserves, (2) supports short-lived soft reservations for low-latency requests, (3) applies graceful demotion when credits run low (route to smaller/quantized model variants or throttle), and (4) exposes metrics and tracing to validate fairness and SLO compliance. The vault will integrate with the existing admission controller and routing layer and be region-aware for spillover and burst absorbtion.

Why different from prior approaches: instead of hard per-tenant hard caps or FIFO deprioritization, the vault models transient capacity as fluid credit that ages and can be borrowed across short windows. This reduces unnecessary rejections and enables controlled preemption of free-tier work with minimal latency impact to paid lanes.
acceptance_criteria: Credit vault created and persisted in Redis with TTL-based aging and per-plan soft/reserve thresholds configured via Console
Admission controller consults vault before routing; paid/enterprise requests should be admitted at >95% rate under typical load while free admission drops first under congestion
When credits for free tier fall below threshold, free requests are transparently demoted to quantized-model variant with documented quality delta
Dashboard shows credit utilization, admission rate per plan, and per-region spillover events
Automated e2e test that simulates a burst and asserts paid/enterprise p99 latency remains within SLO with >99% pass
Fallback policy defined and tested: model-variant downgrade -> queue-delay -> 429 when all fallbacks exhausted
work_notes: 2025-02-15: Kickoff sync with runtime and routing teams. Scoped vault data model and APIs. Action: Marco to prototype Redis-backed reservoir (ETA 1 week).
2025-02-20: Prototype completed. Using ZSET per-plan with credit tokens represented as timestamps for aging. Initial microbench shows 7k ops/s at 50ms median latency for vault check on local infra.

2025-02-25: Design decision: prefer optimistic fast-path (no RPC to vault for cached warm keys) with conservative fallback to explicit vault check for region spillover. Trade-off: slightly more complexity in cache invalidation but reduces median admission latency.
2025-02-28: Integrated with admission controller. Added feature flag 'adaptive-vault-enabled' per-region. Running internal canary against us-west-2 with 10% of traffic.

2025-03-02: Canary observed expected behavior: free admission down 60% during synthetic burst, paid/enterprise admission unchanged. Logged recommendation to add sarama-based metrics exporter to reduce steal on hot ZSET keys.
2025-03-03: Addressed race condition where simultaneous borrow and replenish could oversubscribe vault; implemented simple compare-and-del on token pop. Added unit tests and updated e2e harness.
Next: finalize console controls and add canary increment plan. Plan for incremental rollout tied to runtime-1.22 milestone.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Vault becomes single-point hotspot for popular region/plan -> Mitigation: shard keys by region+bucket and use local LRU cache for microbursts
Risk: Quality regression after demotion to quantized variant -> Mitigation: preflight evaluation dataset to estimate ROUGE/embedding distance before rollout and gated A/B tests
Risk: Unexpected billing edge-cases (credit borrowing across pay-period boundaries) -> Mitigation: bookkeeping at commit-time and conservative cap on cross-window borrow
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): enable in 1 region for 10% of requests. Monitor admission rates and p99 latency for paid plans.
Phase 2 (regional expand): enable across 3 regions with traffic ramp to 30%. Add console controls for soft-reserve per plan.
Phase 3 (global): enable by default, expose feature toggle and contingency rollback script to revert to hard-quota mode within 5 minutes.
Post-release: run 2-week fairness audit and collect customer-reported incidents
